title: Reviewing Income Criteria for Student Care Fee Assistance to Reduce Out-of-pocket Expenses
what_it_is: Reviewing Income Criteria for Student Care Fee Assistance to Reduce Out-of-pocket Expenses

sections.label: SCFA subsidies and fees
sections.summary: ComCare families get maximum SCFA subsidies; median SCFA family pays $29 per child, highest subsidy pays $5, while SCC median fee is $295.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Families receiving ComCare Financial Assistance automatically qualify for maximum SCFA subsidies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Around three in five families on SCFA receive maximum subsidies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: The median family receiving the SCFA pays out-of-pocket fees of $29 per child.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Those receiving the highest subsidy pay as low as $5.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: The median fee for SCCs without assistance is $295 and has remained stable over the past few years.

sections.label: SCFA review and startup grant
sections.summary: SCFA was last enhanced in 2020 and is reviewed periodically; per capita income is considered for larger families, and a startup grant covers initial enrolment costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: To the first point, the SCFA was last enhanced in 2020 and we do review it from time to time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: For larger families, we do look at the per capita income condition, so that each family, if they do qualify, they can qualify for higher subsidies where plausible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: The Member rightly said that the SCFA is not meant for enrichment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: There is perhaps one component that I did not mention and that is the startup grant, and that helps the families to pay for initial enrolment costs – things like buying a mattress, putting in centre deposits, buying uniforms, for instance.
